report:
Native liver, total hepatectomy

Received fresh is a native liver weighing 1240 g and measuring 21 x 15 x 9 cm. The hilar margins (bile duct, portal vein and hepatic artery) are submitted en face. The gallbladder is attached. Four hilar lymph nodes are identified. The liver is serially sliced at 5 mm intervals. The parenchyma is bile-stained. No mass or prominent nodule is seen. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

(1) Hilar margins en face.
(2-3) Hilar bile ducts.
(4-9) Background liver.
(10) Gallbladder.
(11) Hilar lymph nodes.

The liver shows established cirrhosis (Ishak stage 6/6). Periductal concentric fibrosis, bile duct loss and copper-associated protein are present. There is low-grade biliary intraepithelial neoplasia. Four hilar lymph nodes show reactive changes. The gallbladder shows chronic cholecystitis. There is no malignancy.

LIVER, native, total hepatectomy - PRIMARY SCLEROSING CHOLANGITIS with CIRRHOSIS (Ishak stage 6/6); LOW-GRADE BILIARY INTRAEPITHELIAL NEOPLASIA
